dangote-refinery-2024.summary: In January 2024 Dangote Petroleum Refinery in Lekki Free Zone east of Lagos began producing diesel and jet fuel from Nigerian crude, after a decade of construction, a cost near US$20 billion and a single crude distillation unit rated at 650,000 barrels a day. Petrol followed in September 2024, when state oil company NNPC began lifting it under a naira-for-crude arrangement. Nigeria, Africa's largest crude producer, had imported nearly all refined fuel while its four state refineries stood idle. Disputes over crude supply, pricing, import licences and a 2025 fuel import tariff followed, and Dangote reported full-capacity test runs in February 2026.
